newsitem.title: USA: US spot propane continues to sag in thin talk.
newsitem.headline: US spot propane continues to sag in thin talk.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices sagged in thin talk late on Friday as trade was deadened by a computer failure in a market already scarce of players because of the extended Christmas holiday.
Players said a computer trading program used by many traders went down in the afternoon and by later today was still out in many offices.
Forecasts for warm weather expected to last until January 4, also put a damper on values, traders said.
Spot propane in the Midwest trading hub of Conway, Kansas, fell about one cent to between 72.75 cents and 73.00 cents a gallon.
Mont Belvieu prices fell about one cent to 52.75/53.00 cents.
Meanwhile, some traders were quoting rumors that Koch Oil was preparing to start up its Sterling pipeline that has been down since August because of an explosion.
A company source, however, said they were eyeing the third week in January for opening the 35,000 barrel per day (bpd) capacity line.
The damaged line is one of two in the Sterling system that feeds customers in the Gulf Coast from staroge facilities in Mont Belvieu, Texas.
((-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631))
